subject: Dedicated capacity: overflow allowance & autoscale playbook
content:
From: Elaine Park <elaine@bluehaven.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Jimenez <c.jimenez@bluehaven.ai>
Date: 2029-11-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing questions for our Q1 ramp

Jonas —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Were close to finalizing the commitment for a dedicated pool, but before we sign we need to align on how overflow/bursting will be handled during launch. Two quick asks:

1) In week 1 of launch we expect a 4x spike over baseline for inference traffic for a 48-hour window. Can you confirm the headroom policy youd recommend and how preemptible/spot capacity would be used?

2) We need a clear autoscale cooldown/backfill and mutex policy so our SREs know when to push traffic vs. hold.

Attaching a sample traffic pattern (see CSV) — happy to jump on a call.

—Elaine
Senior Product Ops, Bluehaven Analytics


On Nov 02, 2029, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:

> From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
> To: Elaine Park <elaine@bluehaven.ai>
> Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
> Date: 2029-11-02T11:03:00-08:00
> Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing questions for our Q1 ramp
>
> Elaine — thanks for the clear asks. Ive looped Monica (CS ops) to own the sizing workbook and laid out a short plan below. Ill schedule a 30-min kickoff for Monday to walk the matrix.
>
> Quick summary of our approach:
> - Baseline reserve: we recommend 20% static reserve for steady-state critical workloads.
> - Short-window overflow: for transient spikes (<=72h) we offer an overflow allowance that combines reserved shoulder capacity, preemptible GPUs, and controlled ephemeral slab capacity.
> - Fallback: when primary capacity is saturated we route lower-priority jobs to preemptible nodes with a tokenized backfill window and graceful throttle.
>
> I attached the Dedicated_Sizing_Workbook_v1.xlsx. Monica will propose the exact headroom numbers after reviewing your CSV.
>
> Cheers,
> Jonas
> VP, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference


On Nov 03, 2029, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com> wrote:

> From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
> To: Elaine Park <elaine@bluehaven.ai>
> Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
> Date: 2029-11-03T10:21:00-08:00
> Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing questions for our Q1 ramp
>
> Hi Elaine / Carlos —
>
> Per the workbook review (attached) here are proposed guardrails based on your 4x spike scenario: 
>
> 1) Headroom & reserve model (recommended)
> - Steady-state baseline: size for 95th percentile of pre-launch traffic + 20% static reserve.
> - Launch-window headroom: provision a separate ephemeral shoulder slab sized to absorb 1.5x the 95th percentile for the first 72 hours.
> - Overflow allowance: allow automatic preemptible capacity up to 40% of total pool for temporary absorption; this is billed at preemptible rates and carries a lower availability SLO.
>
> 2) Autoscale policy (defaults we will set in Dedicated config)
> - Scale-up trigger: sustained 5-minute CPU/GPU utilization > 70% OR queue depth > 30 requests for two consecutive 1-minute windows.
> - Scale-down cooldown: 15 minutes (no aggressive shrink during launch windows).
> - Backfill window: when preemptible nodes are reclaimed, we will keep preemptible-backed tasks in a graceful backfill queue for up to 10 minutes and then shift to reserved throttles.
> - Mutex/priority rules: critical inference routes (token flag: critical=true) always get routing priority to reserved slab; best-effort routes are eligible for preemptible backfill.
>
> 3) Throttle behavior and graceful failure modes
> - Soft throttle at 90% effective capacity: return 429 with Retry-After for stateless non-critical calls and queue tokens for stateful work.
> - Hard reject at 110% oversubscribe to protect model quality pipelines.
>
> Action items for Bluehaven:
> - Confirm the set of routes that must be flagged critical (weve annotated a suggested list in the workbook).
> - Confirm whether you want a 30% or 40% preemptible cap (we suggested 40% above for launch flexibility).
>
> Ive attached Autoscale_Throttle_Matrix.csv that encodes the cooldowns and triggers so your SREs can consume it programmatically. Also adding SLA_Addendum_Draft.pdf for the overflow allowance language — Ben will follow up on contractual wording.
>
> Happy to jump on a call to walk through the policy table.
>
> Best,
> Monica
> Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
>

On Nov 04, 2029, Elaine Park <elaine@bluehaven.ai> wrote:

> From: Elaine Park <elaine@bluehaven.ai>
> To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
> Cc: Carlos Jimenez <c.jimenez@bluehaven.ai>
> Date: 2029-11-04T08:46:00-08:00
> Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing questions for our Q1 ramp
>
> Monica — this is great level of detail. A couple of clarifying Qs before we finalize: 
> 1) On the backfill window: if preemptible capacity is reclaimed during a high-priority burst, do you have an escalation path to temporarily borrow reserved capacity from other shoulder slabs? Were worried about losing critical calls mid-run.
> 2) Who will be the on-call escalation for P0 capacity incidents during launch days? We want a single Slack/phone contact.
>
> Also — can you confirm the billing delta well see if we use 40% preemptible vs 30%? Id like an estimate for the SOW.
>
> Thanks,
> Elaine


On Nov 06, 2029, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com> wrote:

> From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
> To: Elaine Park <elaine@bluehaven.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
> Date: 2029-11-06T15:04:00-08:00
> Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing questions for our Q1 ramp — final alignment
>
> Hi Elaine / Carlos — following internal alignment here are the firm commitments and next steps we agreed on: 
>
> - Borrowing policy: during critical P0 bursts we will enable temporary cross-slab short-term borrowing up to 10% of other shoulder slabs within the same region (manual emergency escalation with ops approval). This requires a signed SLA addendum (attached).
> - On-call: Redwoods launch-day escalation will be Ben Carter (on-call lead) + a 24/7 escalation path to our infra runbook. Ill share the direct pager in the DocuSign envelope.
> - Billing delta: switching from 30% -> 40% preemptible cap reduces committed billing by ~11% on modeled launch traffic (see workbook tab "cost-model"). Exact SOW numbers will be in the contract amendment.
>
> Next steps:
> 1) Bluehaven to confirm critical routes by EOD 2029-11-08.
> 2) Ben to send DocuSign for SLA_Addendum_Draft.pdf and the addendum for backfill/borrowing.
> 3) Monica to schedule the launch runbook rehearsal (we recommend one dry-run 72 hours before go-live).
>
> Links: HubSpot (deal) https://hubspot.company.com/deals/BH-2029-112 | Drive folder with workbook https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3Cdrive | DocuSign https://app.docusign.com/templates/abc-123
>
> Thanks — were excited to partner on this.
>
> Cheers,
> Ben Carter
> Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
>
> Attachments: SLA_Addendum_Draft.pdf; Dedicated_Sizing_Workbook_v1.xlsx; Autoscale_Throttle_Matrix.csv
